events.date_basis: FOMC statement released October 28 at 14:00 EDT (October 29 at 03:00 JST); Tokyo cash bond market had closed
events.title: FOMC holds 3.75-4.00% target range (10-2 vote)
events.summary: The FOMC maintained the federal funds target range at 3.75-4.00% on October 28 by a 10-2 vote; two members preferred a 25bp increase. This is U.S. policy context for JGB and yen monitoring, not a BoJ decision.
events.caveat: Official release is October 28 U.S. Eastern time; displayed on October 29, the first subsequent Tokyo session. Chart placement does not establish a causal JGB or yen response, or the size of any Fed surprise.

events.date_basis: Decision at October 29-30, 2026 MPM, dated October 30 in Japan; no intraday market timing inferred
events.title: BoJ maintains 1.25% overnight rate and increases ETF disposal pace
events.summary: At its October 30 MPM, the BoJ kept the uncollateralized overnight call rate around 1.25% by an 8-1 vote and unanimously raised the annual ETF sale pace from about JPY330bn to about JPY860bn on a book-value basis, to be implemented in January 2027.
events.classification: Policy-rate hold and faster planned ETF disposals
events.caveat: The ETF change was decided October 30, not implemented that day; the official statement specifies January 2027 without an exact day. No future rate decision, intraday market effect or realized ETF sale is inferred.

sources.title: Bank of Japan: Statement on Monetary Policy (October 30, 2026)
quotes: The Bank will encourage the uncollateralized overnight call rate to remain at around 1.25 percent.
and set the pace of sales at about 860 billion yen per year (on a book value basis).
The change will be implemented in January 2027.

events.date_basis: BLS released October-reference-month CPI on November 10 at 08:30 EST (22:30 JST), after Japan's cash market closed
events.title: U.S. October CPI: headline +0.4%, core +0.3% m/m
events.summary: BLS published October 2026 CPI on November 10: all-items CPI rose 0.4% month over month, seasonally adjusted, and CPI excluding food and energy rose 0.3%. The data are October price changes released in November.
events.classification: U.S. inflation data — not a rate decision
events.caveat: Released November 10 at 08:30 EST, after the Tokyo close; marker placed on the November 11 Tokyo session. No CPI surprise or causal JGB/yen response inferred. BLS cannot publish most October 2026 12-month rates owing to unavailable October 2025 indexes.

sources.title: BLS: Consumer Price Index, October 2026
quotes: The index for all items less food and energy rose 0.3 percent in October, as it did in September and August.
